notes: All four assigned rows have identical study, description, and p. 5 locator. These identify the paper and broad exposure relationship but do not distinguish exposure class, duration category, adjusted versus unadjusted analysis, or duration versus cumulative-dose and cancer-subtype analyses. No row-specific test can be assigned without guessing. Table 2 printed adjusted OR candidates (all versus <1 year of the corresponding exposure): prolactin-increasing 1–4 years 1·04 (95% CI 0·79–1·36), ≥5 years 1·56 (1·27–1·92); prolactin-sparing 1–4 years 0·95 (0·73–1·25), ≥5 years 1·19 (0·90–1·58). Table 2 also prints unadjusted ORs and any-antipsychotic comparisons. Results on this page additionally report cumulative ≥5000 DDD adjusted OR 1·36 (1·09–1·70) for prolactin-increasing and 1·15 (0·84–1·58) for prolactin-sparing exposure; cancer-subtype ≥5-year adjusted OR candidates are 2·36 (lobular) and 1·42 (ductal). The p<0·0001 on p. 887 belongs specifically to adjusted OR 1·56 for ≥5 years prolactin-increasing exposure versus <1 year, not to every candidate. The abstract gives the weaker p<0·001 bound for that same comparison; retain the page-5 printed bound as candidate. Table 2 common sample headers are 5339 controls and 1069 cases; these remain candidates only because row-specific test correspondence is unresolved. No total N is calculated or extracted. Methods p. 885 says controls could become cases later, so the header counts are not asserted to be mutually exclusive unique women. Exclusions: previous cancer except non-melanoma skin cancer, organ transplant, mastectomy, HIV before index/matching date; histologically verified first invasive breast cancer, age 18–85; controls matched by age and time since schizophrenia diagnosis. Source title and DOI match the assigned original primary paper. PDF p. 5 rendered and visually inspected. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
